newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Bond market, govt differ on SAfrica reforms - paper.
newsitem.headline: Bond market, govt differ on SAfrica reforms - paper.

text.p: South African bond traders are unhappy at the speed with which the government wants to implement market reforms, including shortening the settlement period, Business Day newspaper reported on Monday.
The government has proposed changing bond market settlement to T+3 (settlement three days after trade), from the current system of settlement by the second Thursday after trading day.
The paper quoted Bond Exchange acting chief executive Grant Page as saying the exchange had asked traders for more comment on the proposal.
He confirmed that bond dealers had expressed unhappiness with the government's urgency in implementing the reforms.
The Reserve Bank has said traders' suggestion of a November 13 changeover was too late, and proposed instead that August be set as a target.
Some dealers are believed to be critical too of the government's plan for a new system of auctioning its stock to private market makers during the current fiscal year.
Reasons for wanting to shorten the settlement period include reducing perceived credit risk, which the government believes is keeping foreign players from entering the local market.
But dealers said a Bond Exchange risk management system being put in place would achieve the aim of reducing risk.
Shortening the settlement period would be expected to have a dramatic effect on volumes, with reduced activity by speculators.
